example.title: Stretched quadrupole ion trap (3D Paul trap)
example.reference: R. E. March, "An introduction to quadrupole ion trap mass spectrometry", J. Mass Spectrom. 32, 351–369 (1997), worked example (Calculations)
example.summary: Hyperboloid ring and endcaps of the commercial ion trap, with the endcaps moved out by 10.6 % ("stretched"), driven as in the paper's worked example for butylbenzene (m/z 134). Compare the Trap tab's q_z and axial frequency with the paper's.
published: ring r₀ = 1.00 cm; endcaps at z₀ = 0.783 cm (2z₀ = 15.66 mm), electrode shapes those of the unstretched trap
V = 757 V (0-p) on the ring at Ω/2π = 1.05 MHz, U = 0, endcaps grounded
0.318 from β_z ≈ q_z/√2, "high by about 5 %" at this q
assumptions: Electrode truncation: ring hyperboloid out to |z| = r₀, endcaps out to the same radius (not stated).
The endcaps are the unstretched hyperboloids 2z² − r² = r₀² moved out along z by 0.783 − 0.707 = 0.076 cm.
